page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7571 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores clocked at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The compute configuration is matched with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. In addition to general compute and memory resources, this instance includes 300 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD local storage, providing low-latency temporary block storage without requiring standalone network-attached volumes for scratch space. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no dedicated GPUs are attached.

Benchmark results reflect the older generational characteristics of the AMD EPYC 7571 silicon. Single-threaded performance sits in the lower tier, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 728.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 591.09. Multi-threaded compute results are modest, yielding 2952.0 in Geekbench and 2361.03 in stress-ng. However, memory subsystem tests demonstrate stable operational capability, with PassMark memory scoring 1929.27 and PassMark overall CPU scoring 6909.38, supported by hardware cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI achieving 6495.82 in encryption tests. Storage-coupled and memory-centric throughput benchmarks indicate steady handling for standard data structures, such as Redis SET throughput at 5.03 million operations per second and static web serving at 5.07 GB/sec.

The primary operational tradeoff of the m5ad.2xlarge centers on CPU instruction set limitations and raw clock speed. The processor lacks AVX-512 extensions and exhibits lower memory bandwidth compared to contemporary platforms, making it unsuited for intensive mathematical modelling, modern AI training, or dense compression jobs. The primary value lies in its balanced resource allocation paired with integrated fast local NVMe storage. It functions well as a cost-effective platform for persistent application workloads, intermediate build servers, caching nodes, staging databases, and general web services requiring local scratch disks without peak single-thread execution speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an 8-vCPU AMD EPYC 7571 processor at 2.2 GHz and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration alongside 300 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing places single-core and compression capabilities in lower performance tiers, while overall PassMark CPU and memory benchmarks demonstrate stable mid-range consistency for standard compute tasks. Because it includes integrated high-speed local disk alongside standard memory allocations, this instance provides dependable utility for general-purpose application workloads, development and testing environments, staging databases, and caching tiers that benefit from fast local temporary storage but do not require heavy floating-point vector calculations.
